content:
Following the May I/O 2026 preview, Gemini for macOS is now rolling out advanced voice control features.

Google positions this functionality as letting you 「speak naturally in any window on your desktop」, with two main capabilities.

The first is smart voice input, which transcribes 「dictated words into clean, polished text」. Gemini automatically removes filler words like 「um」 and 「ah」, while capturing the key point you want to convey based on mid-sentence corrections.

The formatted text is entered at your current cursor position. This will provide a voice-to-text experience similar to the upcoming Gboard Rambler for Gemini Intelligence on phones.

The other capability goes beyond simple transcription, understanding your current screen content to execute complex tasks. This opt-in feature requires you to enable Gemini reasoning in the app's settings.

  • Extract and summarise data: Highlight local files, images, or documents on your desktop, then tell Gemini what you need. For example, you could say: 「Read these veterinary records and write a summary of my dog's medical history as an email to the boarding facility.」
  • Write and rewrite text: Highlight text anywhere on screen, then use voice to instantly rewrite, adjust the tone, and place the polished version exactly where you need it. Try saying: 「Rewrite these notes as an executive summary with a TL;DR at the top.」
  • Generate and edit images: Use voice to create visual content, whether brainstorming concepts, enriching travel itineraries, or making quick modifications based on designs on your desktop. Try saying: 「Generate a dark mode version of this illustration.」

Long-press the Fn key anywhere on macOS to launch, or click the new screen share button at the end of the 「Ask Gemini」 prompt box. Gemini will display a floating capsule-shaped icon with sound waves at the bottom of the screen.

Please ensure you've updated Gemini for macOS to the latest version (1.88). This new voice feature is rolling out globally, currently supporting English, with more languages 「coming later」.
